data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English word 'cald' meaning 'vigorous' or 'strong' and 'well' meaning 'valley' or 'spring'. The name Caldwell was given to children born in a strong or famous valley, or to those who were considered strong or famous themselves. The name Caldwell carries the meaning “Famous, strong one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Caldwell usually hope their child will grow to embody famous, strong one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_english.name: Caldwell
in_english.meaning: English surname of Celtic origin, possibly derived from the words 'cold' and 'well'.
in_english.long_meaning: Caldwell is an English surname of Celtic origin, possibly derived from the words 'cold' and 'well'. It is believed to have originated from the Old English words 'cald' and 'well', which together mean 'cold spring' or 'source of water'. The name is commonly found in England, particularly in areas with warm springs and wells. It is thought to have been originally a topographic name, indicating the location of a cold spring or well.

data.cultural_impact: The name Caldwell is rooted in Anglo-Saxon or Old English traditions. "Cald" signifies strength or vigor, suggesting someone with an indomitable spirit. This invokes images of a mighty warrior or a courageous explorer setting out to conquer new territory. The name's Celtic origins also tie it to ironworking, as the word "cald" was used to describe the hot metal in the forge. This historical significance could lend a sense of creativity, adaptability, and passion to the bearer of this name.
